Residency index of each animal, at each station or in the array

Source: R/summarise_detections.R
residency_index.Rd

The residency index is the share of days an animal could have been detected on which it was detected. Its denominator counts only days on which a receiver listened, from the receiver listening table (see audit_listening()), within the animal's period: from its release, or its first detection when the release is unknown, to its last detection. A day with a detection counts as a listening day whatever the table says, because a detection proves the receiver worked, so the index is at most 1.

Usage

residency_index(x, by = c("station", "animal"))

Arguments

x

A detset(). Its listening table is used as it stands; run audit_listening() first to drop days on which receivers failed.

by

"station" for one row per animal and station, or "animal" for one row per animal over the whole array.

Value

A data frame with animal_id, station_id (by station), days_detected, days_listening (the denominator), days_period (all days of the animal's period) and residency (days_detected / days_listening). With no detection that has an animal_id, it has no rows, and a message says so.

Details

Appert et al. (2023) found two main forms of the index in 72 studies: days detected over days at liberty, and days detected over the monitoring period. This function uses the first form, with the period ending at the last detection. Counting only the days on which a receiver listened is this package's own rule; it keeps receiver outages out of the denominator. The function is named residency_index() so that it does not mask actel::residency(), an unrelated analysis.

References

Appert, C., Udyawer, V., Simpfendorfer, C. A., Heupel, M. R., Scott, M., Currey-Randall, L. M., Harborne, A. R., Jaine, F., and Chin, A. (2023). Use, misuse, and ambiguity of indices of residence in acoustic telemetry studies. Marine Ecology Progress Series 714, 27-44. doi:10.3354/meps14300

See also

summarise_animals()

Examples

study <- detqc_example
dets <- detset(study$detections, study$deployments, study$animals)
head(residency_index(dets, by = "station"))
#>   animal_id station_id days_detected days_listening days_period residency
#> 1     ST-01       S001             5              9           9 0.5555556
#> 2     ST-01       S002             4              9           9 0.4444444
#> 3     ST-01       S003             4              9           9 0.4444444
#> 4     ST-01       S004             1              9           9 0.1111111
#> 5     ST-01       S005             1              9           9 0.1111111
#> 6     ST-01       S006             2              9           9 0.2222222
head(residency_index(dets, by = "animal"))
#>   animal_id days_detected days_listening days_period residency
#> 1     ST-01             9              9           9         1
#> 2     ST-02             9              9           9         1
#> 3     ST-03             8              8           8         1
#> 4     ST-04             9              9           9         1
